quick_consumer_choose.description: Existing consumers retain their stable IDs.

quick_consumer_basics.title: Consumer – power and priorities (1/4)
quick_consumer_basics.description: A three-phase 6 A charger at 230 V requires approximately 4,140 W minimum. Different devices have different limits.

quick_consumer_output.title: Consumer – control output (2/4)
quick_consumer_output.description: Choose an existing HA entity, including a native Modbus write number. Add a new Modbus write point under Advanced settings first if needed.

quick_consumer_conversion.title: Consumer – convert W to A
quick_consumer_conversion.description: All internal budgets remain in W; outputs in A are rounded down to configured actuator steps.

quick_consumer_feedback.title: Consumer – feedback and demand (3/4)
quick_consumer_feedback.description: Without a measured power sensor actual load is unknown. Without a demand switch, demand is always yes.

quick_modbus_setup.title: Modbus setup
quick_modbus_setup.description: Create a connection first, then configure and repeatedly test a read sensor in the same form.

quick_data_points.title: Manage data points
quick_data_points.description: Create, test and edit Modbus read sensors in one place. Write actuators are configured separately; read tests never send commands. Existing Home Assistant entities can be assigned under Site or Consumers.

quick_connections.title: Manage Modbus TCP connections
quick_connections.description: A connection can be reused by multiple sensors and actuators. Connection and data point are separate objects.

quick_read_point_choose.title: Choose Modbus read sensor
quick_read_point_choose.description: Create a new sensor or edit an existing sensor. Editing preserves its identifier.

quick_read_point_form.title: Modbus read sensor – configure and test
quick_read_point_form.description:
**Latest test result:** {result}

You can edit any field and test again. A successful read test is required before saving. Successful communication does not guarantee the decoded value is physically correct. Testing **never writes or saves anything**.
